title: feat(scheduling): S-SCHED-2 authoritative booking lifecycle, no double booking, assignment-gated reads, real booking push (T4)
body:
## Tier header

**Tier:** T4 (T3 elements included)

**Why:** This PR changes who can read scheduling data. Session types, availability and open slots are now limited to the client's assigned coach(es). Session reads are limited to participants. Client views drop coach-only fields. It also adds a database constraint and edits one CI workflow line.

**T4 trigger scan:**
- Read-access change: yes. `SchedulingAccessService` limits client reads and bookings to the head coach plus an active sub-coach assignment (open `SubCoachAssignment` with a non-archived `TeamSubCoachAssignment`). `GET /scheduling/sessions/:id` is participant-only and returns 404 `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` to anyone else. Client views null out `coach_notes_md`, `provider_idempotency_key`, `video_meeting_id` and `calendar_event_id`, and hide `video_url` while a request is pending.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: one additive change that adds `test/scheduling-booking-concurrency.live.spec.ts` to the mwb-3-live-tests jest list, plus a comment. No job, gate or permission changes.
- New table: none, so no new RLS. `SessionType` and `CoachingSession` keep their existing enabled and forced RLS (PR-RLS-03). The new columns inherit it.
- `scripts/ci/*` and schema-parity-baseline: untouched.

**T3 trigger scan:**
- Concurrency and state authority: per-coach advisory lock, in-transaction re-validation, compare-and-set transitions.
- Persistent schema: migration `20270222000000_scheduling_lifecycle_integrity` with `down.sql` (S-SCHED-3 adds reminder delivery-state columns to `NotificationDeliveryLog`, a range preflight and the `btree_gist` ownership marker; id unchanged).
- Cross-repo contract: the mobile client consumes it in #325.
- Shared notification primitive: the `BookingEmitter` rewrite.

**Bounded T1:** none.

**Builder-owner:** agent 110 (Claude Opus 5.5 builder), lane S-SCHED-2; fix round S-SCHED-3 by agent 111 (builder); fix round S-SCHED-4 by agent 112 (Claude Opus 5.5 builder); round 3 (S-B3) by sub-manager 114-S builder lane (Claude Opus 5.5). Not self-audited.

**Acceptance evidence:** see the Tests section below.

**Reminder switch (operator decision):** #624 recorded "ships on; only off disables". This PR and #632 make unset mean off, so reminders stop on deploy unless `BOOKING_REMINDERS_ENABLED=on` is set. Recommended: set it through the B-FLAGS manifest in the same deploy window.

**Promotion triggers:** any change to the access predicate, the exclusion constraint, the occupying-status set, the transition fence (status + start_at + end_at), the reminder claim/lease semantics, or the reminder switch semantics re-opens T4 review.

## What changed

### 1. Authoritative validation on request and reschedule
The server now validates every request and reschedule, regardless of what the client sends:
- `session_type_id` is required (`SESSION_TYPE_REQUIRED`). The type must be active and owned by the coach (`SESSION_TYPE_UNAVAILABLE`).
- The duration must equal the type's duration (`DURATION_MISMATCH`). Times must be whole minutes.
- Lead time is at least 5 minutes (`SESSION_IN_PAST`). The horizon is at most 120 days (`BEYOND_BOOKING_HORIZON`).
- The interval must sit inside the coach's availability windows. Windows can be type-scoped. Overrides apply: holiday, block and extra hours (`SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`). Containment is checked over merged free ranges (`isIntervalBookable`).
- Each type is either instant-confirm (`auto_approve`, goes straight to `scheduled` with `approved_at` set) or needs coach approval (`requested`).
- A client can have at most 3 pending requests per coach (`PENDING_REQUEST_LIMIT`) and one upcoming welcome booking per coach (`WELCOME_ALREADY_BOOKED`).
- When a client moves a confirmed session of an approval-type, it goes back to `requested` for the coach to approve again. A coach move is checked for overlap but may fall outside open hours (5–480 minutes).
- Reschedule clears the `NotificationDeliveryLog` reminder rows, so the reminders fire again for the new time.

### 2. No double booking
- **Service layer:** booking writes run in a READ COMMITTED transaction. Each one first takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock('schd' namespace, hashtext(coach_id))`, then re-reads everything. Writers for one coach are serialised; readers are not blocked.
- **Database floor:** a new exclusion constraint, `CoachingSession_no_overlapping_active_booking EXCLUDE USING gist (coach_id WITH =, tsrange(start_at,end_at,'[)') WITH &&) WHERE status IN ('requested','scheduled','pending_provider')`. Pending requests hold their slot. Back-to-back sessions are allowed.
- **Error mapping:** a constraint violation or serialization failure returns 409 `SLOT_TAKEN`. Lock or pool timeouts return 503 `CALENDAR_BUSY`.
- **Transitions:** approve, decline, cancel, complete, no-show and reschedule are compare-and-set on the booking revision (status, start_at, end_at, plus the start boundary). If the status changed underneath, the response is 409 `SESSION_STATE_CHANGED`; if the same-status session moved to a new time, it is 409 `SESSION_MOVED`. Approve, decline, cancel and no-show accept an optional `expected_start_at` (the time the caller saw); a mismatch is `SESSION_MOVED` before any write. Notifications are built from the committed row.
- **Provisioning (S-SCHED-3):** the provider write-back is fenced on the revision and the link fields. A manual link saved meanwhile is kept, a cancel, decline or move wins, an obsolete confirmation is not sent, and a calendar event or meeting created for a superseded revision is cancelled (audit `SESSION_PROVIDER_CANCELED`, reason `superseded_revision`). Cancelling a session also cancels its provider artifacts. A client cannot cancel after the start (`SESSION_STARTED`). Complete and no-show require the session to have started.

### 3. Contracts and ownership
- `GET /scheduling/my-coaches` returns head coach first, then sub-coach. Each entry has name, avatar, timezone, relationship and `bookable_type_count`. It also has `welcome { session_type_id, name, duration_minutes, active_session_id, active_session_status, active_session_start_at, completed_at }`.
- `GET /scheduling/coaches/:id/open-slots?session_type_id=` returns slots sized to the type. It respects type-scoped windows and filters by lead time and horizon. Results are cached per type and the cache is cleared on any availability or override write.
- `SessionType.is_welcome` is the persistent welcome marker. A partial unique index allows one active welcome type per coach, and marking a new one clears the old.
- `SessionType.default_meeting_url` is a per-type default link. It must be https (enforced by the API and a CHECK constraint). It is used when the video provider gives no link, and it is hidden from clients in the type list.
- `GET /scheduling/sessions?scope=past&before=&before_id=` lists past sessions newest first; `scope=upcoming` (default) pages with `after=&after_id=`. Keyset on `(start_at, id)`, so tied start times are neither skipped nor repeated. Optional `status=requested,scheduled,...` filter. An unreadable cursor or filter is 400 `INVALID_LIST_QUERY`.
- `SessionView` adds `session_type`, `coach_name`, `client_name`, `meeting_link_status` (`ready|pending|awaiting_approval|none`), `cancellable` and `reschedulable`.
- Every failure returns a stable `code` and a plain message that says what happened and what to do next. Codes: `SESSION_TYPE_REQUIRED`, `SESSION_TYPE_UNAVAILABLE`, `DURATION_MISMATCH`, `SESSION_IN_PAST`, `BEYOND_BOOKING_HORIZON`, `INVALID_TIME`, `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`, `SLOT_TAKEN`, `CALENDAR_BUSY`, `PENDING_REQUEST_LIMIT`, `WELCOME_ALREADY_BOOKED`, `SESSION_STATE_CHANGED`, `SESSION_NOT_ACTIVE`, `SESSION_STARTED`, `COACH_NOT_BOOKABLE`, `COACH_NOT_FOUND`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `NOT_SESSION_PARTICIPANT`, `INVALID_MEETING_LINK`, `SESSION_MOVED`, `INVALID_LIST_QUERY`.

### 4. Notifications
- Each lifecycle event writes one in-app row and sends a real push via `NotificationsService.pushToUser`. Events covered: requested, confirmed (instant or approved), booked (coach side of an instant booking), declined, cancelled, moved, move requested, link needed and link ready.
- Push respects `muted` and `booking_push`.
- Both the in-app row and the push carry `actionScreen` and `actionParams.sessionId`, so a tap opens the session. Clients go to `CalendarSession` and coaches to `CoachBookingInbox`. These match the mobile `pushTapRouter`.
- Times are shown in the recipient's own timezone with the zone abbreviation.
- 24h and 1h reminders use the same transport. They now include `pending_provider` sessions. The `BOOKING_REMINDERS_ENABLED === 'on'` line is identical to #632 (merged into this branch).
- **Reminder delivery (S-SCHED-3):** a claim is a `sending` row with a 4-minute lease and a claim token. Only P2002 means "already claimed"; any other claim error counts as a failure and is retried. Each channel is settled separately (`inapp_done_at`, `push_done_at`), so a retry resends only what failed and the retried push links the first in-app row. Expired leases are taken over; live leases are left alone. A claim made for a different start time is a new revision. Each session is re-read before sending, and a cancel or move in between releases the claim. Preference suppression and a missing device are settled answers. After 3 attempts the row is `gave_up` with `last_error`.
- **Missing meeting link:** when a session is confirmed without a link, the coach gets a "link needed" prompt. The coach's reminders say "Add one so they can join". The client reminder says "Your coach will add the call link before it starts". Attaching a manual link notifies the client and moves a `pending_provider` session to `scheduled`.

## Migration and operator preflight
`20270222000000_scheduling_lifecycle_integrity` (prefix per the operator correction at 22:44) does the following, and is reversed by `down.sql`:
- Adds the two `SessionType` columns, the welcome partial unique index and the https CHECK.
- Creates `btree_gist` in the `extensions` schema when that schema exists, otherwise in the default schema.
- Runs a preflight that **refuses** to apply while overlapping active rows exist. It never cancels or moves anyone.
- Runs a range preflight (S-SCHED-3) that **refuses** to apply while an active row ends before it starts, instead of failing on a bare tsrange error.
- Adds the exclusion constraint.
- Marks `btree_gist` with an ownership comment only when this migration installed it; `down.sql` drops the extension only when the marker matches and nothing else depends on it (otherwise a NOTICE and it stays).
- Adds `NotificationDeliveryLog` delivery state: `status` (default `sent`), `attempts` (default 1), `lease_until`, `claim_token`, `session_start_at`, `inapp_done_at`, `push_done_at`, `notification_id`, `last_error`, plus `NotificationDeliveryLog_status_check`. Existing rows read as sent once, so the deploy re-sends nothing.
- S-SCHED-4: adds index `NotificationDeliveryLog_kind_status_idx` on (`kind`, `status`) (also `@@index([kind, status])` in schema.prisma) for the per-tick recovery read; `down.sql` drops it. Migration id unchanged (20270222000000; main's latest is 20270216000000).

### Pre-deploy checks (operator runs both, read-only; each must return zero rows before the migration deploys)
Overlaps:
```sql
SELECT a.coach_id, a.id AS session_a, b.id AS session_b,
       a.status AS status_a, b.status AS status_b,
       a.start_at AS a_start, a.end_at AS a_end, b.start_at AS b_start, b.end_at AS b_end
FROM "CoachingSession" a
JOIN "CoachingSession" b
  ON a.coach_id = b.coach_id AND a.id < b.id
 AND a.status IN ('requested','scheduled','pending_provider')
 AND b.status IN ('requested','scheduled','pending_provider')
 AND a.start_at < b.end_at AND b.start_at < a.end_at;
```
Inverted ranges (S-SCHED-3):
```sql
SELECT id, coach_id, status, start_at, end_at
FROM "CoachingSession"
WHERE status IN ('requested','scheduled','pending_provider') AND end_at < start_at;
```

## Merge order and overlap
- Based on main (`7a6cfd82`), not stacked on another PR.
- `git merge-tree` against #632 (`0ae744b6`), #607 (`e8feb0d2`) and #609 (`5fd61a1b`) merges cleanly in every case. The `ci.yml` line is placed away from #607's insertion on purpose.
- #632's reminder switch lines are identical here.
- Follow-up from #632 done in S-SCHED-4: the C04 seed creates "Quick initialization" with `is_welcome: true` unless the coach already has an active welcome type.
- S-SCHED-4 merged main `3bd6215b` (merge commit `b5e6e62d`, tree equals `git merge-tree 2a07ab25 3bd6215b`; no hand edit). No new env reads (BOOKING_REMINDER_1H_CRON / BOOKING_REMINDER_24H_CRON / BOOKING_REMINDERS_ENABLED are already in ENV_RULES).
- #607 and #609 do not touch `SessionType` or `CoachingSession`.

## Tests
Targeted runs, each via `ops/heavy.sh npx jest <files> --runInBand`:
- **New:** `test/scheduling-lifecycle-integrity.spec.ts`, `test/booking-emitter.spec.ts` (rewritten), `test/scheduling-reminder-delivery.spec.ts`, `test/slot-computer-bookable.spec.ts`, `test/scheduling.service.spec.ts` (moved onto the shared typed harness, which removes untyped fakes and casts), and `test/booking-reminder.job.spec.ts` (fake now handles `status: { in }`).
- **Neighbours, unchanged:** availability-overrides, slot-computer, scheduling-permissions, qa-p0-launch-blockers, entitlement-guards-mounted, notification-emitters, notification-prefs, dunning-v2 route table and guard, scheduling-providers, openapi-spec, route-doc-drift, roles.guard, lockscreen-privacy, push-preference-defaults, google-calendar.service. All pass.
- **What the tests prove:**
  - The race tests use a fake DB that models the lock and the exclusion constraint. They include a control case showing the harness *does* double-book when both guards are off.
  - The live spec runs against real Postgres. It applies the migration from its file, checks the preflight refuses overlaps, and checks that a direct overlapping insert or re-activation is rejected and recognised by the mapper. It runs 6 concurrent requests and gets 1 row plus 5 `SLOT_TAKEN`. It holds the advisory lock in a third transaction and shows both bookings waiting on it, then exactly one commit. It runs approve against cancel and gets exactly one winner. Locally it skips (no Postgres); it runs in the mwb-3-live-tests job.
- **Static checks:**
  - tsc (`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3584`) at head: exit 0.
  - prettier and eslint on changed files: clean.
  - `node scripts/check-r75.js --mode=range --base=origin/main --head=HEAD`: OK. `as any` −1, `as unknown as` −2, `as never` −1.

## Risks
- **Client behaviour change:** a booking without `session_type_id` now gets 400 `SESSION_TYPE_REQUIRED`, and clients can no longer browse coaches outside their assignment. Mobile #325 is updated in the same lane. Native scheduling stays behind the mobile `clientCalendar` flag.
- **Migration on prod:** it will refuse to apply if overlapping active rows exist. Run the preflight query above first.
- **`down.sql`:** it drops `btree_gist` only when this migration installed it (ownership comment) and nothing else depends on it. A pre-existing extension is left in place. Rolling back drops the reminder delivery-state columns but keeps the claim rows, so nothing is re-sent.
- **Approval-type move (C-634-4, disclosed):** a client moving a confirmed approval-type session still gives up the original time when it goes back to `requested`. Mobile #325 now warns before the move. Holding the original until the coach answers is an owner product decision (follow-up).
- **Schema parity:** Prisma does not model the partial unique index, the CHECK or the exclusion constraint. This follows the existing `ImportIntent_one_current_key` precedent, where Prisma's differ ignores partial indexes. The Schema parity check is the arbiter.
- **Reminders stay off** until an operator sets `BOOKING_REMINDERS_ENABLED=on`.

### S-SCHED-4 fix round (finding -> change -> commit -> test)
All 8 new cases in `test/scheduling-lifecycle-integrity.spec.ts` (`S-SCHED-4 B-634-2`) fail on the `2a07ab25` reminder job and pass on `d1661ab8`; they advance the fake clock by the real cron interval instead of re-running at the same clock.

| Finding | Change | Commit | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| B-634-2 (Sol, residual) recoverable rows stranded when the next tick leaves the band | `dispatchWindow` also reads its kind's unfinished rows (`retry`, or `sending` with an expired/null lease; oldest first, bounded 200/tick) independently of the band; re-verifies session status, the claimed start revision and that the recipient is still a participant; re-sends only unfinished channels and only to recipients with unfinished work (no new claims outside the band); the band pass keeps sessions that are back in band. Work that can never be sent is closed as `gave_up` with `last_error = retired:<reason>` by compare-and-set (session_cancelled, session_started, superseded incl. a 24h reminder once the 1h band is reached, recipient_changed, attempts_exhausted incl. a dead worker's 3rd attempt); receipts kept. ### S-SCHED-5 fix round (Sol re-audit @ `d1661ab8`, comment 5960774667) (finding -> change -> commit -> test)
Sol's three executed probes (`ops/aud-sol3-112/backend634-independent-boundaries.spec.ts`, `AUD-SOL-3 reminder recovery failure boundaries`) are now regression tests in `test/scheduling-lifecycle-integrity.spec.ts` (`S-SCHED-5 B-634-2 / B-634-6`). 7 of the 8 new or changed cases fail on the `d1661ab8` reminder job / seed and pass at `4d987916`. The late-booking case passes on both: it guards the new catch-up pass (log `ops/s-sched5-112/failing_before.log`).

| Finding | Change | Commit | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| B-634-2a (Sol) first-claim failure: no row, so recovery never sees it | New catch-up pass in each sweep (`collectMissedFirstClaims`). It reads confirmed sessions in `[lower - 30 min, lower)` (and past the 24h 65-min cutoff), keeps those confirmed (`approved_at`, else `created_at`) at least `lowerOffset` before start, so a late booking is never sent a back-dated reminder, and claims only participants with **no** row of that kind.
